1 About GlobalTrust Financial Services

GlobalTrust Financial Services (GTFS) was established in 2012 in Singapore with a clear mandate: to build a financial institution that combines the rigour of traditional banking with the agility of modern technology. What began as a mid-sized commercial lender with fewer than 200 employees has evolved, over fourteen years, into a diversified multinational financial services group employing 4,850 professionals across four strategic markets

1 About GlobalTrust Financial Services

- Singapore, Dubai, Mumbai, and London.

From its inception, GTFS has pursued a disciplined growth strategy anchored in three principles: sustainable financial performance, customer-centric service delivery, and technology-led innovation. The organisation has consistently reinvested a substantial proportion of its annual operating surplus into infrastructure modernisation, talent acquisition, and digital capability-building, resulting in a robust, scalable operating model that positions GTFS competitively across both emerging and mature markets. The Group's digital transformation journey, formally launched in 2019 under the banner of Horizon 2025, delivered significant milestones including the migration of core banking operations to the proprietary Atlas platform, the rollout of a fully integrated mobile banking suite, and the implementation of an enterprise-wide data analytics infrastructure. GTFS is today recognised within the Asia-Pacific financial services sector as a technology-driven institution capable of competing with both incumbent banks and emerging fintech challengers.

RECOGNITION

GTFS ranked among the Top 10 Most Innovative Financial Institutions in Southeast Asia for three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025) by the Asian Banking & Finance Institute.

5 Business Units

5 Business Units

Retail Banking The Retail Banking division serves individual customers and small businesses across GTFS's branch network and digital channels. Offering current and savings accounts, personal loans, credit facilities, and payment solutions, Retail Banking is the primary interface between the Group and its broad consumer base. The division manages over 620,000 active retail accounts and processed more than 48 million transactions in FY2025. Commercial Banking Commercial Banking caters to mid-market enterprises with annual revenues between SGD 5 million and SGD 250 million. Services include trade finance, working capital facilities, cash management, and structured lending. The division maintains dedicated relationship management teams in each of the Group's four regional offices, enabling localised service delivery underpinned by global credit standards. GlobalTrust Financial Services Corporate Banking The Corporate Banking unit addresses the complex financing needs of large corporations, government-linked entities, and multinational clients. Product coverage spans syndicated lending, project finance, debt capital markets advisory, and cross-border transaction banking. Corporate Banking maintains formal coverage relationships with over 310 corporate clients across Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. Mortgage Services Mortgage Services provides residential and commercial property financing solutions to retail and institutional clients. The division offers fixed- and variable-rate mortgage products, equity release facilities, and property refinancing. Automation of origination workflows, currently underway as part of the FY2026 Mortgage Automation Initiative, is expected to reduce application processing time by 60%. Wealth Management The Wealth Management division delivers personalised investment advisory, portfolio management, estate planning, and discretionary asset management services to high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals. With assets under advisory exceeding SGD 4.2 billion, the division operates under a fiduciary model with rigorous suitability and best-interest obligations. Treasury Operations Treasury manages the Group's balance sheet, liquidity, and market risk exposures. Responsibilities include foreign exchange operations, interest rate risk management, interbank lending, and regulatory capital optimisation. The Treasury desk operates across time zones, providing 24-hour coverage across the Singapore, Dubai, and London offices. Risk & Compliance The Risk & Compliance function serves as the second line of defence across all business lines. It encompasses credit risk, market risk, operational risk, financial crime compliance, AML/KYC oversight, and regulatory reporting. The division maintains active relationships with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), and the Financial Conduct Authority

(FCA).

Information Technology The IT division is the operational backbone of GTFS, responsible for the Atlas Core Banking Platform, enterprise infrastructure, software development, system integration, and IT service management. The division leads the Group's cloud migration programme and oversees the development of Project Phoenix - GTFS's internal AI-powered knowledge management system. GlobalTrust Financial Services Digital Banking Digital Banking drives the Group's consumer-facing technology strategy, including the GTFS Mobile App, internet banking portal, open banking APIs, and digital onboarding. The division is responsible for product innovation, user experience design, and the expansion of the digital customer base, which grew 34% year-on-year in FY2025. Customer Experience The Customer Experience division owns the end-to-end client journey across all touchpoints - branch, digital, telephony, and correspondence. It manages the Group's Net Promoter Score programme, complaint resolution framework, and service quality benchmarks. Current initiatives include the rollout of an AI-assisted contact centre platform and a redesigned digital self-service portal. Human Resources Human Resources supports a workforce of 4,850 employees across four countries, encompassing talent acquisition, learning & development, performance management, compensation & benefits, and employee relations. The HR division is spearheading the Group's Future of Work programme, which includes hybrid work policy governance, leadership development pipelines, and diversity & inclusion initiatives. 8 Technology Landscape

8 Technology Landscape

Technology is the principal enabler of GTFS's competitive strategy. The Group's technology estate has been substantially modernised over the past five years and continues to evolve in alignment with the FY2026 Strategic Plan. Key components of the technology landscape are described below. Atlas Core Banking Platform Atlas is GTFS's proprietary, cloud-ready core banking platform, purpose-built to support the Group's multi-product, multi-currency, and multi-jurisdictional operating model. Deployed in 2021 following a three-year implementation programme, Atlas serves as the system of record for all banking products, customer accounts, and financial transactions. The platform processes an average of 2.1 million transactions per day with 99.97% system availability. Enterprise Data Analytics Platform The Group's data analytics infrastructure consolidates structured and unstructured data from across all business units into a centralised data lake, enabling real-time reporting, predictive modelling, and regulatory analytics. Business intelligence dashboards are available to all senior management and business heads through the GTFS Insights Portal. Project Phoenix - Internal AI Knowledge Assistant Project Phoenix is a Group-wide initiative to develop and deploy an AI-powered knowledge management assistant for internal use. The system is designed to enable employees to retrieve policy documents, procedural guidance, compliance information, and institutional knowledge through a natural-language interface. Phoenix is currently in controlled pilot across the Risk, Compliance, and HR divisions, with a full enterprise rollout planned for Q2 2026. GlobalTrust Financial Services Cloud Infrastructure GTFS operates a hybrid cloud model, leveraging approved private and public cloud environments for non-core workloads while maintaining critical banking systems on managed on-premise infrastructure. Cloud Migration Phase II, running through FY2026, targets a 75% cloud-hosted workload ratio by December 2026, subject to MAS cloud outsourcing requirements. Cybersecurity Programme The CISO-led cybersecurity programme encompasses a Security Operations Centre (SOC) providing 24/7 threat monitoring, a vulnerability management lifecycle, penetration testing, phishing simulation, and mandatory security awareness training for all staff. GTFS maintains certifications under ISO 27001 and aligns with the MAS Technology Risk Management (TRM) Guidelines and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. GlobalTrust Financial Services
9 Corporate Governance

9 Corporate Governance

GlobalTrust Financial Services maintains a rigorous corporate governance framework aligned with the standards prescribed by its primary regulators and the principles of the Singapore Code of Corporate Governance. Governance responsibilities are clearly delineated across the Board of Directors, the Executive Committee, and independent oversight functions. Board Oversight The Board of Directors, comprising seven members including four independent non-executive directors, provides strategic direction and oversight of the Group's activities. Board committees include the Audit Committee, Risk Committee, Nomination & Remuneration Committee, and the Technology & Innovation Committee. The Board meets no fewer than six times per annum. Risk Management GTFS operates a Three Lines of Defence risk governance model. Business units constitute the first line, owning and managing risks within their operations. The Risk & Compliance function serves as the independent second line, setting frameworks and challenging risk-taking. Internal Audit serves as the third line, providing independent assurance to the Audit Committee. Regulatory Compliance The Group maintains active regulatory relationships with four primary regulators: the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), and the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). All regulatory submissions, capital adequacy filings, and compliance certifications are managed through the Group Compliance function under the Chief Risk Officer. Internal Audit The Internal Audit function operates independently of management and reports directly to the Board Audit Committee. The function conducts risk-based audits across all business units, technology systems, and control environments on a rolling annual cycle. All audit findings and management action plans are tracked through the Group's GRC platform.

11 Future Outlook

11 Future Outlook

GlobalTrust Financial Services enters FY2026 from a position of organisational strength, underpinned by a robust capital base, a modernised technology infrastructure, and a workforce that is increasingly digital-first in its capabilities and mindset. The strategic priorities adopted by the Board reflect a clear-eyed assessment of both the opportunities and the challenges inherent in the current macroeconomic and regulatory environment. The adoption of artificial intelligence across the enterprise represents the most transformative opportunity available to GTFS in the near term. Project Phoenix, when fully deployed, will fundamentally alter how employees access, share, and apply institutional knowledge. Beyond Phoenix, the Group is actively evaluating the application of machine learning in credit underwriting, fraud detection, customer segmentation, and regulatory reporting - all domains where data-driven decisioning has the potential to deliver material improvements in accuracy, speed, and cost-efficiency. Automation remains a core operational lever. The Mortgage Automation Initiative and the Operational Efficiency Programme are expected to collectively deliver over SGD 22 million in annualised cost savings by FY2027. These savings will be partially reinvested into customer-facing enhancements, talent development, and the continued build-out of the Group's digital banking infrastructure. Automation will not displace the Group's workforce but will redeploy human capital toward higher-value advisory and relationship-driven activities. Geographic expansion remains a medium-term priority. The Board has authorised a feasibility study for a representative office in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, reflecting the significant commercial banking opportunities emerging from Vision 2030 and the broader Gulf region's economic diversification agenda. Additionally, the Group is reviewing options for a digital banking licence in one further Southeast Asian market, most likely Malaysia or Indonesia, subject to regulatory prerequisites. The ongoing evolution of the digital banking landscape - including the proliferation of open banking frameworks, embedded finance, and real-time payment rails - will require GTFS to maintain an accelerated GlobalTrust Financial Services pace of product development and technology investment. The launch of the GTFS Super App in Q3 2026 is expected to be a defining moment for the Group's retail banking proposition, consolidating banking, payments, wealth, and insurance services within a single, intuitive customer interface. Customer trust remains the Group's most valuable and most carefully protected asset. In an era defined by data breaches, operational failures at peer institutions, and heightened consumer expectations around security and transparency, GTFS's commitment to zero regulatory breaches, best-in-class cybersecurity practices, and proactive client communication constitutes a genuine competitive differentiator. The Group's NPS of +58 - among the highest in its peer group - reflects the tangible returns of this long-term investment in trust and reliability. Looking ahead, the Group's leadership is committed to ensuring that GTFS remains a financially sound, technologically advanced, and purpose-driven institution - one that delivers sustainable value to shareholders, meaningful opportunity to employees, and genuinely impactful financial services to the communities it serves. The foundations built over the past fourteen years position GTFS well to navigate an increasingly complex global landscape and to continue earning the trust of clients, regulators, and partners alike.

FY2026-FY2028 STRATEGIC TARGETS

The Group's FY2026-FY2028 Strategic Plan targets compound annual revenue growth of 12-15%, a cost-to-income ratio of below 48% by FY2028, and a digital banking penetration rate exceeding 80% of the active retail customer base. GlobalTrust Financial Services
